entries.title: socket — Low-level networking interface — Python 3.15.2 documentation
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'Python socket module documentation settimeout create_connection exceptions socket.timeout' on docs.python.org: first result at this URL with this title; text: socket.timeout is a deprecated alias of TimeoutError since 3.10; create_connection resolves both IPv4 and IPv6 and tries each address in turn; settimeout(0) means non-blocking. Companion result: 'ssl — TLS/SSL wrapper for socket objects — Python 3.15.2 documentation' (docs.python.org/3/library/ssl.html).
entries.version: Python 3.15.2 documentation (the /3/ address follows the newest release)
entries.notes: Authority for the Day 9 TCP service checker and its error tests. Catch TimeoutError rather than socket.timeout in new code. The checker's IPv6 behaviour follows from create_connection trying every resolved address. The guest may run an older interpreter; name the tested version in the lesson.

entries.title: pcap-filter(7) man page
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'tcpdump man page pcap-filter manual' on tcpdump.org: first result 'pcap-filter(7) man page' at this URL; text: filter expressions are built from primitives with type, dir and proto qualifiers, for example 'tcp port 21'. The index www.tcpdump.org/manpages/ was also returned.
entries.version: online copy documents libpcap 1.11.0-PRE-GIT per the result text
entries.notes: Capture-filter syntax (tcpdump, dumpcap), which differs from Wireshark display filters. The online page describes a development version; keywords such as vxlan are newer than the guest's libpcap, so the local man page takes precedence.

entries.title: Firewall - Ubuntu security documentation
entries.access_note: Public documentation page returned by the search without any sign-in or price.
entries.evidence: Query 'Ubuntu Server documentation firewall ufw nftables how-to security' on ubuntu.com and documentation.ubuntu.com: first result 'Firewall - Ubuntu security documentation' at this URL; companion result 'nftables - Ubuntu security documentation' at .../firewall/nftables/; text: ufw is a front end that invokes the legacy iptables and ip6tables utilities and should not be used together with native nftables rules; 'nft list ruleset' lists all rules.
entries.notes: Basis of the Day 9 before-and-after firewall test on the isolated guest. Pick ufw or native nftables, not both. The test must cover IPv6 as well as IPv4, because a rule set that filters only one family leaves the service reachable over the other.

Same result list: 'RFC 1035: Domain names - implementation and specification' (www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc1035/, STD 13, November 1987) and the standards index naming RFC 9293 (TCP, STD 7, August 2022).
entries.notes: Primary standard for the TLS explanation of Day 7; read the handshake overview only. The page of RFC 9293 (TCP) itself was not in a result list, so it is cited here by number only. Later updates to these RFCs were not checked.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Section 5, Week 2 lab specification: a limited Nmap scan uses '-sT -sV --version-light'.

plan_fact_checks.claim: Section 5, Week 2: do not infer that a service is absent solely from the state 'filtered'.
plan_fact_checks.evidence: nmap.org/book/man-port-scanning-basics.html ('Port Scanning Basics') in search results: filtered means Nmap cannot determine whether the port is open because packet filtering prevents its probes from reaching the port; the six states describe how Nmap sees a port, not an intrinsic property of it.
